description:
**Divergence**: every extension-server sibling has a tests/max_objects_in_set.rs integration test except calendars-server.

| Crate | tests/max_objects_in_set.rs |
|---|---|
| mail-server (canonical) | YES |
| chat-server | YES |
| tasks-server | YES |
| contacts-server | YES |
| filenode-server | YES |
| metadata-server | YES |
| sharing-server | YES |
| **calendars-server** | **NO** |

**Caller-observable / maintainer effect**: the canonical mail-server test (and its 6 mirrors) exercises the JmapBackend::max_objects_in_set default and the dispatcher's enforcement of it. Calendars-server has no equivalent test — a future regression where calendars-server's dispatch skips the max-objects-in-set check, or where a custom backend's override is silently ignored, has no in-workspace tripwire.

Likely an accidental sweep gap when the canonical pattern was propagated; this is exactly the kind of asymmetric coverage gap the canonical-template rule is supposed to prevent.

**Fix**: copy crate-jmap-tasks-server/tests/max_objects_in_set.rs (smallest sibling at ~140 lines, mostly cookie-cuttable) into crate-jmap-calendars-server/tests/max_objects_in_set.rs, adjusting per-method to use Calendar/set, CalendarEvent/set, etc. instead of Task/set.

**Cross-references**: bd:JMAP-ops7.3 (calendars-server handler-fn naming outlier, closed). Calendars-server has accumulated cookie-cutter drift in two distinct axes — handler naming and test coverage. Worth a calendars-server-only sweep epic if a third axis surfaces.
title: calendars-server missing tests/max_objects_in_set.rs that the other 7 extension-server crates carry
